registration_scope: The aggregate n2/n3 disagreements and sublevel ratios were already known. This protocol is recorded before the new process-level ablation and rate-block substitution outcomes; it is not a blinded discovery experiment.

hypotheses.claim: Different intensity normalization, electron density, finite depth or quadrature accounts for the discrepancy.
interventions: Record actual gas density, electron density, temperature and incident spectral convention in both codes.
Repeat Cloudy thickness and frequency refinement, and escape frequency refinement.
Evaluate populations at matched fixed electron density before comparing charge-coupled roots.
hypotheses.discriminant: Changes must exceed the measured numerical uncertainty and remove the disagreement under the same atomic rates; converged code flags alone do not test this hypothesis.

hypotheses.claim: Missing n=3 orbital-angular-momentum mixing is a substantial contributor.
interventions: Measure Cloudy n=3 mixing rates and the n3s/n3p/n3d source budgets.
Add or remove only the n=3 mixing block at fixed other rates and fixed electron density, then repeat with charge conservation.
If a Cloudy switch also changes n=2 mixing, label it a confounded intervention rather than a clean n=3 ablation.
hypotheses.discriminant: Compare all three sublevels and total n3; movement toward statistical sublevel ratios alone does not establish total-population agreement.

hypotheses.claim: The shell-only Kramers approximation differs materially from l-resolved photoionization and inverse recombination data.
interventions: Compare each level's photoionization and radiative recombination coefficients at matched irradiation and temperature.
Substitute the photoionization and inverse recombination block together, preserving a consistent inverse-process convention.
Separate fixed-ne and charge-coupled population responses.
hypotheses.discriminant: Use rate and source-budget differences to attribute the population change; a simultaneous fit of unrelated coefficients is not an attribution test.

hypotheses.claim: Bound-bound or collisional-ionization data contribute independently of orbital mixing.
interventions: Compare transition-by-transition collision coefficients and ionization/three-body pairs.
Swap the remaining collisional block separately from n=3 mixing and bound-free rates.
hypotheses.discriminant: Retain pairwise inverse-process checks and identify whether a change affects fixed-ne populations or acts through electron-density feedback.

hypotheses.claim: Different retained shells, collapsed-level conventions, cascades or top-off account for part of the mismatch.
interventions: Verify resolved/collapsed levels and top-off settings rather than comparing nominal nmax labels alone.
Compare nmax4 and nmax5 separately before increasing atom size.
Keep atomic truncation adequacy separate from matched-finite-atom code agreement.
hypotheses.discriminant: Agreement at equal atom size does not establish convergence to a larger or infinite atom.

attribution_rules.contributor: A controlled intervention changes the discrepancy by more than the independently measured numerical uncertainty, with other blocks held fixed.
attribution_rules.dominant: A single controlled block explains at least 80 percent of the initial absolute n3 discrepancy and restoring the block restores that discrepancy. Otherwise report contributors and interactions without declaring a sole cause.
attribution_rules.implementation_error: Distinguish a solver or convention bug from deliberately different atomic data by solving the same recorded rate system independently.
attribution_rules.data_adoption: Adopt a change only with a stated equation/source and applicability, not merely because it lowers the population error.

repair_loop: Reproduce the failed baseline and retain its exact inputs, executable/source identity and outputs.
Select an unresolved hypothesis and record a discriminating intervention before running it.
Execute the intervention; retain unsuccessful attempts and confounding changes.
Record a scoped attribution assessment and a Decision to change data, physics, numerics or the hypothesis.
Implement the selected change and run conservation, detailed balance, derivative and numerical-refinement checks.
Repeat the unchanged external-reference criteria at both atom sizes and at explicitly declared held-out conditions.
If criteria still fail, inspect the remaining rate/source budgets and continue with another justified intervention.

completion_policy.agreement_complete: The declared observables meet the unchanged external-reference tolerance at both atom sizes and all explicitly recorded validation conditions, with numerical and derivative checks passing.
completion_policy.blocked: Record the specific unavailable information or invalid physical comparison that prevents a discriminating next experiment; report a bounded unresolved result, never relabel it as agreement.
completion_policy.scope: This protocol closes the controlled code-comparison investigation only; atom-size convergence, transonic flow and KELT-9b accuracy remain separate claims.
